title: US Measles Cases Pass 5,182, Highest in Decades, as Deaths Rise Nationwide
excerpt: The CDC reported 5,182 confirmed measles cases as of November 5, more than double last year's total, with Pennsylvania passing 1,400 cases and state health departments reporting eight measles-associated deaths this year.
body:
• The CDC reported 5,182 confirmed US measles cases as of November 5, 2026, up 330 in a week and more than double the 2,289 cases in all of 2025.
  • Of this year's cases, 562 people, or 11%, were hospitalised, and 96% of infections were in people who were unvaccinated or whose vaccination status was unknown.
  • Pennsylvania has the largest outbreak, surpassing 1,400 cases, and states reported three measles-associated deaths in a single week in Pennsylvania, New York and Wisconsin.
  • Reader check: confirm you and your children are up to date on the MMR vaccine — two doses are 97% effective — and check the CDC measles page before travel to outbreak areas.

The resurgence of measles in the United States has far surpassed a three-decade high, doubling last year's case count and causing multiple deaths as the country approaches an international review of its measles elimination status.

The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention reported 5,182 confirmed measles cases in the United States as of November 5, USA Today reported. Reuters reported the same CDC figure on Friday, noting it was up 330 cases from the previous update.

The numbers behind the surge

As of November 5, the CDC reported 5,182 confirmed cases in 45 states plus Washington, D.C., more than double last year's total of 2,289. Of those, 562, or 11%, were hospitalised, according to both USA Today and Reuters.

People aged 20 and older accounted for 2,132 cases, followed by 2,104 cases among those aged 5 to 19 and 908 cases in children under 5, Reuters reported from the CDC data. A total of 4,993 cases, or 96% of infections, were linked to outbreaks, and 43 outbreaks have been reported so far this year.

Almost all illnesses, 96%, were contracted by unvaccinated people or those with unknown vaccination status, USA Today reported. Measles is so contagious that 90% of unvaccinated people who are exposed to it contract the disease, according to the CDC figures cited by USA Today.

Contagion Live's November 6 update added that the count rose 6.8% in a week from 4,852, and that this year's total is the highest annual count since 1991. The CDC's measles cases and outbreaks page is the federal source for the weekly figures.

Pennsylvania at the centre, deaths in three states

Pennsylvania, now the epicentre of the nation's largest outbreak, confirmed its sixth measles-related death of the year on November 4, while New York announced its first in 30 years on November 2. Wisconsin also reported on November 5 that an infant had died, its first measles death since 1990.

"It is with a heavy heart we are reporting the first death of an infant connected with a measles outbreak in Wisconsin in many years," Wisconsin Department of Health Secretary Kirsten Johnson said in a news release quoted by USA Today. "Any death of a child is a tragedy and even more so when it is related to a vaccine-preventable disease."

As of November 4, Pennsylvania's infections had surpassed 1,400, according to state health data cited by USA Today, up from 106 cases reported statewide last year. Contagion Live reported the sixth Pennsylvania death involved an unvaccinated Jefferson County resident who tested positive for measles, with the state declining to release further details, citing privacy laws.

State health departments have now reported eight measles-associated deaths nationwide in 2026, although the CDC's official count stands at four, Contagion Live noted. USA Today reported the CDC count, which lags state reporting, reflected four deaths as of October 29, amid a dispute over how measles-related deaths are classified.

Elimination status under review

Measles was declared eliminated in the United States in 2000. The World Health Organization is expected to review the US status on November 10, following the 2025 Texas outbreak that killed three people, USA Today reported. Canada already lost its measles-free status in November 2025.

The MMR vaccine, which protects against measles with 97% efficacy, is typically given at ages 12 to 15 months for the first dose and ages 4 to 6 for the second, USA Today reported. For families in the US, including recent arrivals whose children's immunisation records may be from another country, this is the moment to verify MMR status with a doctor or school, especially before travel to states with large outbreaks.
